title: Discharged for migraines; his marriage
summary: He was in about a year and a half and got out on migraines; he describes marrying in Chicago, his second marriage.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, how long did that last?
Well, I was in there for about a year
and a half, something like that. I would have been in longer, but then they told me I couldn't get out. Said this camp was one of the camps that you just couldn't get out of the Army like that.
But I got out, I got out.
Somebody told you what to do?
Well, not exactly. It was -- I had those migraine headaches, and that got me out of the Army, see.
Oh, yeah. Thank God for that. Yeah.
So what was that, like about '42? '43?
Yeah, that was in '43.
No, wait a minute. You joined the Army in '43.
Yeah, right.
You know what? This says -- oh, and then you went with the Jesse Miller band in Chicago?
That was after I got out of the Army.
Well, how did that happen?
Well, when I got out of the Army, I came back to New York.
Incidentally, Gus, were you married then?
Yes.
You got married in Kansas City?
No, I got married in Chicago. A little
town right out of Chicago.
Oh.
And she knows the name of the town.
I can't think of that little town.
Yeah.
This is my second marriage.
Yeah, yeah. And -- I see, so then when you got out, you went back to Chicago.
No, I went back to New York. She was in New York.
Oh, I see, I see.
At least, she was in camp with me.
Oh, I see.
She came there during the time I was there, we left together, you see.
Yeah, I see.
She stayed till I got out.
Right. And she went to New York.
When we went back to New York together, right.
